ai-at-work.title: How AI guardrails are impeding the work of offensive cybersecurity researchers
ai-at-work.excerpt: We spoke with several cybersecurity researchers, who look for unknown vulnerabilities and develop tools to exploit them, about how OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s guardrails affect their work.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: AI companies are blocking cybersecurity researchers from using their models to find vulnerabilities and develop exploit tools, even though this is legitimate defensive work. This matters because security researchers rely on access to cutting-edge tools to stay ahead of real threats, and overzealous guardrails are basically handing advantage to the actual bad guys who don't care about OpenAI's policies anyway. It's the classic corporate risk-aversion problem: companies would rather disappoint the good guys than face a headline about misuse, even though that math never adds up in security.

ai-at-work.title: Anthropic updates Claude voice mode with more capable models
ai-at-work.excerpt: Claude's new voice model will let you reschedule your meeting or draft an email.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic rolled out upgraded voice capabilities for Claude that now handle practical workplace tasks like rescheduling meetings and drafting emails. This matters because voice interfaces are becoming the actual way people interact with AI tools at work, and if Claude's voice mode can genuinely handle your calendar and inbox faster than typing, adoption curves shift overnight. That said, I'll believe "more capable" when I see someone actually use this instead of just demoing it at a conference, because nine times out of ten these voice features end up being slower than just doing the thing yourself.

ai-at-work.title: AI chip startup Etched defies skeptics, hits $10.3B valuation from big-name investors
ai-at-work.excerpt: Etched, founded by three Harvard dropouts, has created new chips and memory components that speed up inference on any AI model -- no GPUs required, it says.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Three Harvard dropouts just convinced serious money that they can replace GPUs for AI inference work, landing a $10.3 billion valuation despite plenty of doubters in the market. For digital workplace folks, this matters because whatever Etched actually delivers will reshape the economics of deploying AI tools in your organization, potentially making AI applications cheaper and faster to run at scale. I'll believe it when I see it working reliably in production, but I respect any team willing to bet against the GPU cartel and actually get funded for it.

ai-at-work.title: Salesforce rolls out new Slackbot AI agent as it battles Microsoft and Google in workplace AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: Salesforce on Tuesday launched an entirely rebuilt version of Slackbot, the company's workplace assistant, transforming it from a simple notification tool into what executives describe as a fully powe
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Salesforce rebuilt Slackbot from a basic notification tool into a full AI agent that can search data, draft documents, and execute tasks for employees, now available to Business+ and Enterprise+ customers. This matters because workplace AI agents are becoming table stakes for collaboration platforms, and how well they access your actual enterprise data will determine whether they're genuinely useful or just expensive autocomplete. Honestly, the real test isn't what Slackbot can do in a demo, it's whether it can actually find the right information in your chaotic SharePoint libraries without hallucinating a quarterly forecast.

tools-tech.title: I use Anthropic's Claude AI tools for very different jobs: How to pick between models, Code, and Cowork
tools-tech.excerpt: Here's how Anthropic's AI tools work, what they can accomplish, and why security, cost, and your oversight still matter.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Anthropic released multiple Claude AI tools designed for different tasks, with varying capabilities and price points depending on your use case. Digital workplace pros need to understand which model fits which job because deploying the wrong tool wastes budget and creates security gaps that'll keep your IT team up at night. The real story here is that AI vendors are finally admitting one-size-fits-all doesn't work, which is refreshing, but it also means you actually have to think about what you're doing instead of just clicking the shiny button.

tools-tech.title: AMD raises the AI stakes with Helios, Venice and robotics
tools-tech.excerpt: AMD executives took to the stage at its Advancing AI 2026 event in San Francisco today to detail the company’s next generation of AI infrastructure solutions, from Instinct MI455X AI accelerator GPUs
tools-tech.dwp_take: AMD just announced a full stack of AI hardware and software designed to work together as a unified system, including new GPUs, CPUs, networking gear, and a platform called Helios that ties it all together. This matters because digital workplace leaders are about to face real pressure from vendors to upgrade infrastructure for AI workloads, and AMD is finally offering an integrated alternative to Nvidia's dominant position. Honestly, competition in this space is good for everyone's wallet, though I'll believe "ties it all together seamlessly" when I see actual IT teams make it work.

tools-tech.title: OpenAI Presence raises new questions about enterprise automation and jobs
tools-tech.excerpt: OpenAI has launched Presence, an enterprise service for deploying voice and chat agents that can resolve customer and employee requests, potentially automating some work now handled by frontline suppo
tools-tech.dwp_take: OpenAI just dropped Presence, an enterprise tool that deploys voice and chat agents to handle customer and employee support work that people currently do. For digital workplace leaders, this means you're suddenly responsible for deciding which human jobs to automate, what guardrails to put on AI decision-making, and how to retrain staff who lose their frontline roles. The irony is thick: the same tools promised to make knowledge workers more productive are now the ones potentially replacing them, which should make every digital leader ask themselves whether they're building the future or just outsourcing accountability.

tools-tech.title: Tech layoffs: A 2026 timeline
tools-tech.excerpt: Among a range of factors leading to a wave of tech sector layoffs in 2026 is the rapid rise of artificial intelligence and automation. Companies are reconfiguring their workforces to leverage AI for i
tools-tech.dwp_take: Tech companies are cutting headcount in 2026 largely due to AI adoption and automation, even when their balance sheets look healthy. Digital workplace pros need to understand that the tools they're implementing and supporting are fundamentally changing how many organizations think about their workforce size and structure. Here's the thing: if you're spending 2026 building better collaboration platforms for a company that's simultaneously deciding it needs thirty percent fewer people, you might want to have a conversation with someone in HR about what problem you're actually solving.

digital-culture.title: Employers may no longer have to disclose race and gender data
digital-culture.excerpt: Since 1966, the majority of employers have been legally required to provide a confidential breakdown of their workforce by race and gender to the government. The mandate—which applies to any company w
digital-culture.dwp_take: The Trump administration is rolling back a decades-old requirement for large employers to submit workforce demographic data to the government, eliminating mandatory race and gender reporting that's been standard since 1966. For digital workplace folks, this matters because diversity initiatives, ERG programs, and inclusive hiring tools often depend on solid data to measure progress and identify blind spots in your talent pipelines. Personally, I've never understood how you build better workplaces without actually knowing who works there, but apparently that's considered optional now.

digital-culture.title: Disney layoffs hit Pixar employees, even after the success of ‘Toy Story 5’
digital-culture.excerpt: Several hundred employees were laid off on Tuesday across multiple Disney divisions, including ESPN, National Geographic, Disney Entertainment Television, and Disney Studios. Surprisingly, Pixar staff
digital-culture.dwp_take: Disney just laid off 108 Pixar employees despite the box office success of Toy Story 5, proving once again that financial performance means nothing when Wall Street wants cost cuts. This matters to digital workplace leaders because it exposes the myth that employee engagement, retention programs, and culture initiatives protect your workforce when shareholders demand quarterly wins. Here's the real kicker: you can have the best digital workplace in the world, but if the spreadsheet people upstairs decide they need to slash headcount, your investment in collaboration tools and wellness apps becomes window dressing.

digital-culture.title: The hidden penalty working mothers pay
digital-culture.excerpt: Parental leave looks great on paper, but many working mothers who take it have seen missed promotions, unfair performance reviews, or even job loss. Nearly half of all Equal Employment Opportunity Com
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new Fast Company report shows that despite formal parental leave policies, working mothers face real career penalties including missed promotions, poor reviews, and termination, with pregnancy-related EEOC cases nearly doubling. This matters to digital workplace pros because your policies and culture are only as good as their enforcement, and "great on paper" benefits that don't translate to actual outcomes damage both talent retention and your legal exposure. The uncomfortable truth is that most companies still haven't figured out how to genuinely support working parents without treating them like second-class employees, which is costing them top talent and a whole lot of lawsuits.

digital-culture.title: This new (and very annoying) tactic is forcing RTO companies to let workers work from home
digital-culture.excerpt: Employers have made considerable efforts and obtained remarkable results in asking workers to spend more time in the office over the past two years. But while even complying employees usually regret t
digital-culture.dwp_take: Some workers are deliberately making themselves annoying in the office to force their companies to let them work from home instead. This matters because it signals that heavy-handed RTO mandates are creating perverse incentives, turning workplace culture into a game of chicken nobody wins. After thirty years watching management trends, I can tell you that when employees start weaponizing their own behavior, your RTO strategy has officially failed.

industry-news.title: Reddit Rethinks Google AI Partnership as AI Search Reshapes Publishing
industry-news.excerpt: Reddit's reported review of its Google AI partnership highlights growing publisher concerns that AI-powered search is changing the economics of web traffic. The post Reddit Rethinks Google AI Partners
industry-news.dwp_take: Reddit is reviewing its deal with Google to feed content into AI training after realizing the arrangement might hurt their traffic and revenue in the long run. This matters because digital workplace tools increasingly rely on AI search and content aggregation, meaning your organization's knowledge assets could be similarly commodified without fair compensation. The real kicker is that publishers spent twenty years complaining about Google Search eating their lunch, and now they're getting a second helping with AI doing the carving.

industry-news.title: Apple Fixes Hide My Email Bug After Yearlong Delay
industry-news.excerpt: Apple patched a Hide My Email flaw that could expose real inbox addresses, after a researcher reportedly flagged the issue more than a year earlier. The post Apple Fixes Hide My Email Bug After Yearlo
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple finally patched a Hide My Email vulnerability that exposed users' real inbox addresses, more than a year after a security researcher first reported it. This matters to digital workplace pros because many employees rely on Apple's privacy tools for work email separation, and yearlong delays in security fixes undermine the whole value proposition of those tools. Look, I appreciate Apple's privacy theater as much as the next person, but if you're going to market yourself as the security-conscious alternative, you can't leave critical bugs sitting around for 12 months like yesterday's lunch.

industry-news.title: One Password Mistake Helped Hackers Access Chick-fil-A Account
industry-news.excerpt: Chick-fil-A disclosed a credential stuffing attack affecting customers across 10 states, underscoring the risks of password reuse and account takeover. The post One Password Mistake Helped Hackers Acc
industry-news.dwp_take: A Chick-fil-A employee used a reused password that hackers already had from another breach, giving attackers access to customer accounts across 10 states. This matters to digital workplace professionals because it shows that no amount of fancy security infrastructure stops people from using "Password123" everywhere, which means your employee security training is either not landing or you're not enforcing password managers. After 30 years watching this play out, I can tell you that credential stuffing attacks are basically the digital equivalent of trying every key on a ring, and we're all still handing them an oversized keychain.

industry-news.title: Apple Readies Second-Generation MacBook Neo in Major Mac Lineup Overhaul
industry-news.excerpt: Apple is reportedly testing a MacBook Neo with an A19 Pro chip and 12GB of RAM as shortages and higher prices reshape its broader Mac lineup. The post Apple Readies Second-Generation MacBook Neo in Ma
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple is working on a second-generation MacBook Neo with an A19 Pro chip and 12GB of RAM as it restructures its entire Mac product lineup amid supply constraints and cost pressures. For workplace IT teams, this matters because Mac adoption in enterprises keeps climbing, and understanding Apple's pricing and availability strategy directly impacts budget planning and device refresh cycles. Honestly, if Apple is finally getting serious about a lower-cost Mac entry point, the market might actually start believing that "there's a Mac for everyone" instead of just wealthy everyone.
